gate_verdicts.applied_to: int4 artifacts gated against the fluency thresholds via run_eval.evaluate(gates=...)

group_scale_overhead.scale_dtype_rationale: fp32 scales cost 12 B/row (1.20 MB per 100k-vocab model, 8.0% of the 15.0 MB packed payload); fp16 would save 0.60 MB (3.7% of total) at the cost of a Cast node in every graph and ~0.05% relative scale rounding. fp32 chosen for exact parity with the int8 tier scale dtype and zero extra graph ops.

rust_contract.detail: kotoshu-rs rerank::dequant::RowFormat accepts metadata "int4-per-row" (byte 0x04: packed signed nibbles x ONE fp32 row scale) and its test explicitly rejects "int4-group-128". These artifacts use "int4-group128" + per-group fp32 scales, so kotoshu-rs needs a contract extension: a new RowFormat variant + format byte + the "int4-group128" metadata string, with dequant reusing the existing nibble unpacking (pack_row_int4/dequant_row_int4) and taking ceil(dims/128) fp32 scales per row instead of one; onnx.rs must read the group_scales constant. kotoshu-rs was NOT modified by this experiment.

recommendation:
Do NOT ship int4-group128: rank_corr clears the 0.97 gate on every language (0.9818-0.9885) but top1_agreement fails the 0.95 gate on 8/9 (only ru passes) — 4-bit noise flips roughly 1-2 of the ~30 scoreable typo probes per language, so the fine-grained cosine ordering that the rerank pipeline depends on does not survive at group size 128. int8-per-row remains the shipped recipe. If int4 is retried, the recorded (untried) levers are: smaller groups (64/32), asymmetric unsigned [-8, 15] rounding, or a mixed int4-mini + int8-fluency split. Evidence: eval/reports/int4.{lang}.json.

Retry (2026-09-04): CONFIRMED REJECTION of int4 for full-vocab artifacts: no config in {group 128/64/32} x {nearest-even, half-away} clears the fluency top1 >= 0.95 gate (best canary config int4-g64-ne at min-canary top1 0.8378; ja stays worst at 0.7838); rank_corr passes everywhere, so the 4-bit noise floor keeps flipping 1-2 typo probes per language regardless of grouping or rounding. int8-per-row remains the shipped recipe. The decisive group-32 probe on ja (worst language) still failed (top1 0.9189 ne / 0.9189 ha) at 19005076 bytes. Mixed fallback REJECTED too: int4-mini fails the MINI gate on de.
